description: Club de Ciencia Tecnología y robótica RoboMinds
summary: We develop biomedical software that adapts to each individual and not something one size fits all. For mental health, we think about immediacy in case of an emergency; without needing human intervention, the AI would act as a temporary listener so the astronaut feels heard and a professional can intervene later. The astronauts would have their own autonomy. But also receiving professional help from Earth, our software would help reduce false alerts if, instead of being a single system for everyone, it could adapt to each person as they are and the AI could detect this, unlike other programs.
details: Vigía Vital was born with a clear idea: to create a system that truly understands each person instead of treating everyone the same. Thinking about long space missions or extreme isolation, the project combines real time physical monitoring like electrocardiograms and vital signs with a psychological support space that works completely autonomously. We know that in space or high pressure situations, every second counts that’s why artificial intelligence acts as an immediate temporary listener so the astronaut feels heard and accompanied right away, without having to wait for a response from Earth. At the same time, by learning the unique patterns of each crew member, the software is able to filter out false alarms and help medical teams detect real anomalies. We’ve built all of this using accessible web technologies while always protecting user privacy, keeping their data and medical history safe local in your own browser. More than just a medical tool, we aim to offer a reliable companion that takes care of both body and mind in the toughest environments.
